title: Garden and Letters
premise: Rafael Eastwick ghostwrites the memoirs of celebrity gardener Julian Voss while hiding his own family's crumbling estate and his identity as the estranged Eastwick heir. When his grandmother summons him to a reunion at Ashgrove House, he recruits Wren Calloway, a letter archivist cataloguing his family's papers, to pose as his partner for one weekend. As they read decades of hidden letters together, Rafael realizes the memoir he's writing is built on a stolen family story, and that Wren is falling for the mask, not the man. At the harvest festival, Rafael publicly confesses both his authorship and his feelings, choosing truth over the career that once saved him, and finds that Wren, and a found family of neighbors and relatives, choose him back.
about_author: Bram Ashgrove is the pen name of a former estate archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's love letters before writing any of her own. She lives in a converted greenhouse with too many plants and a typewriter she refuses to retire.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He drafts Julian Voss's memoir by day and hides his own name from every byline, insisting to himself that invisibility is a skill, not a wound. A letter from his grandmother arrives: come home to Ashgrove House for the reunion, or forfeit everything. Emotional beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: An Archivist with Steady Hands
chapters.summary: Rafael meets Wren Calloway, hired to sort the Eastwick family letters, when he catches her reading a 1960s love note meant for no one. Desperate for a date to the reunion, he offers her a bargain: pretend, for one weekend, and he'll grant her full access to the archive. Beat: wary curiosity sparking into mutual intrigue.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She negotiates rules for the fake relationship over coffee, telling herself it's research money, nothing more. They rehearse their story, and Rafael is unsettlingly good at intimacy that isn't real. Beat: the first flicker of doubt about who's performing for whom.

chapters.title: Arrivals at Ashgrove House
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The reunion begins: sharp-tongued cousins, his grandmother's probing warmth, and Julian Voss arriving as an unexpected guest, angling for the Eastwick garden story Rafael has been feeding him. Rafael and Wren must perform their romance under watchful eyes. Beat: tension between belonging and exposure.

chapters.title: Letters in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Escaping the party, they read letters from Rafael's grandfather to a gardener named Iris, discovering a hidden love story the family erased. The fiction between them softens; a near-kiss is interrupted by Julian. Beat: the fake date starts feeling real by dessert, exactly as feared.

chapters.title: What the Memoir Owes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He realizes Julian's bestselling narrative is stitched from the Eastwick letters, stolen through an old assistant, and that finishing the book means publishing his family's heart under another man's name. His editor demands the final chapters by festival's end. Beat: dread hardening into moral crisis.

chapters.title: The Grandmother Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Grandmother Eastwick quietly reveals she has known Rafael was ghostwriting all along, and that she invited him home not to punish him but to make him choose. She gives Wren the last unopened letter, addressed to 'whoever makes him honest.' Beat: permission and pressure entwined.

chapters.title: Midnight, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Wren confronts him: she found the draft memoir and realized their whole weekend sat inside a lie. He confesses everything, the ghostwriting, the theft, the fear of being seen, and she walks out into the dark. Beat: the lowest point; the heart he claimed to contain breaks open.

chapters.title: The Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the festival, with Julian on stage promoting 'his' memoir, Rafael takes the microphone and tells the crowd the book is his, the story is his family's, and the man he loves deserves better than a ghost. Julian storms off; the crowd, and his grandmother, hold their breath. Beat: public climax, costly honesty.

chapters.title: Signed, Finally, in His Own Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the emptied garden, Wren reads him the final letter, which turns out to be from Iris to the family, forgiving them. Rafael signs his real name to a new first page, and Wren kisses him among the late roses. Epilogue beat: inheritance redefined, identity claimed, found family gathered around one table.
